sources.entry: Kanidm | Modern identity management platform written in Rust

summary.one_liner: Kanidm is a self-hosted identity management platform written in Rust that provides identity provider services such as SSO, passkeys, Unix login integration, and LDAP access.
summary.what_it_does: Kanidm is positioned as a complete identity provider so other applications can offload authentication and identity storage to it. According to the README, it supports passkeys (WebAuthn), including attested passkeys for high-security setups, and an application portal for accessing linked apps. It provides OAuth2/OIDC authentication for SSO and token exchange for service access. For Linux/Unix, it offers TPM-protected offline authentication and SSH key distribution, plus RADIUS for network and VPN authentication. It also offers a read-only LDAPs gateway for legacy systems, complete CLI administration tooling, two-node high availability via database replication, and a WebUI for user self-service.
use_cases: RADIUS authentication for VPN or network access
notable: Covers many identity needs in one product (OIDC, passkeys, Unix auth, RADIUS, LDAP gateway) without requiring Keycloak
Built-in database and replication instead of an external SQL database
Two-node high availability using database replication
caveats: Administration is primarily via CLI; the WebUI is designed mainly for user self-service rather than admin tasks, per the README
The README's comparisons are self-described and the performance claims are noted as results that may vary
No install or run instructions are given in the README; it points to the external Kanidm book for documentation
